title: Patricia Abravanel kidnapping turns 25 years
subtitle: Episode in August 2001 involved the student's captivity and the invasion of Silvio Santos' house.
excerpt: Recall the 25‑year anniversary of Patricia Abravanel's kidnapping and the invasion that held presenter Silvio Santos hostage in his São Paulo home.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The series of events that began with the kidnapping of Patricia Abravanel and culminated in the invasion of Silvio Santos' residence turns 25 years old. The incidents, recorded in August 2001 in São Paulo, mobilized public security authorities and inspired the 2024 film 'Silvio'.

The student's abduction in the Morumbi neighborhood

On the morning of August 21, 2001, Patricia Abravanel, then 24, was taken by two armed men dressed in postal uniforms as she left home in Morumbi to go to college. Upon being notified, Silvio Santos contacted the Secretary of Public Security, Marco Vinicio Petrelluzzi, who activated the Anti‑Kidnapping Police Division (Deas). The São Paulo press honored the request to withhold information during the rescue negotiations.

Seven days of captivity and public statements

Patricia Abravanel returned home driving her own car on August 28, 2001, after spending seven days in a hideout located ten kilometers from her residence, following the payment of a ransom. Speaking from her home balcony, she likened the experience to the film "Life Is Beautiful," said she was called a "princess," and declared: "I forgive the kidnappers. I do not forgive the corruption system." Silvio Santos joked: "This daughter gives me an extraordinary headache. I should ask the kidnappers to stay longer with her."

The siege in Alphaville and the invasion of the family home

On August 29, 2001, police located the kidnapping mastermind, Fernando Dutra Pinto, 22, in a flat in Alphaville, Barueri. During the police confrontation, investigators Marcos Amorim Bezerra and Tamatsu Tamaki were killed, another officer was wounded, and the kidnapper escaped through the building's façade.

The next day, August 30, Fernando Dutra Pinto broke into Silvio Santos' house in Morumbi. Íris Abravanel and the daughters managed to flee, but the presenter remained hostage for nearly eight hours. The criminal demanded the presence of the then‑governor of São Paulo, Geraldo Alckmin, as well as a helicopter. After Alckmin arrived to ensure his safety, the kidnapper surrendered his weapons around 2:30 p.m. and released Silvio Santos unharmed.

Judicial convictions and the fate of those involved

Fernando Dutra Pinto was transferred to the Belém Detention Center and died in police custody on January 2, 2002, before trial. On March 11, 2002, Judge Adilson de Araújo sentenced other participants: Esdras Dutra Pinto received 19 years and six months imprisonment, while Marcelo Batista Santos, Luciana Santos Sousa and Tatiane Pereira were each sentenced to 15 years.

With information from O POVO.
